title: The text discusses the alarming decline in life expectancy in sub-Saharan Africa due to the HIV-AIDS epidemic, which has become the leading cause of death in the region. Countries like Sierra Leone, Niger, and Malawi are highlighted for their low healthy life expectancies. The World Health Organization (WHO) has introduced a new measure called Disability-Adjusted Life Expectancy (DALE) to provide a clearer picture of health across countries. In contrast, countries like Japan, Australia, and Sweden rank high in life expectancy due to healthier lifestyles and effective healthcare systems. The text also notes that women generally live longer and healthier lives than men, particularly in wealthier nations, although this gap is narrowing as women's smoking rates increase. Overall, the text emphasizes the disparities in health outcomes between different regions and genders.
